aspects.says: A decision about owned state is made inside the owner's task; a check on a snapshot followed by a submitted change is a check-then-act that lets two callers pass.
basis: section:One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting

aspects.says: With the flag set before the load, a failed load leaves it set and every later call returns null; with the value as its own flag, the next call loads again.
basis: section:A Double-Checked Flag Can Say Loaded Before the Value Is; a synchronized Getter Can't

aspects.says: A double-checked flag kept beside the value can say loaded while the value is null, so a caller during the load gets null; a synchronized getter whose value is its own flag makes it wait.
basis: section:A Double-Checked Flag Can Say Loaded Before the Value Is; a synchronized Getter Can't

aspects.says: A synchronized getter called constantly from many threads costs far more than a volatile-reference double-checked load, which is the fix once a profile shows it.
basis: section:A Double-Checked Flag Can Say Loaded Before the Value Is; a synchronized Getter Can't
aspects.reason: a timing on one machine; both versions are correct, so no deterministic test separates them

aspects.says: State changed only by one owner thread needs no lock, and readers that take an immutable snapshot published after each change see a whole state without waiting.
basis: section:One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting

aspects.says: The owner design costs a hand-off per write and a copy per snapshot; for large, often-changed state a read sent to the owner as a task, or one lock, is cheaper.
basis: section:One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting
section:A Snapshot of 100,000 Bins Copies 800 KB on Every Move
aspects.reason: a throughput comparison on one machine; a graded test can't check a speed ratio deterministically

aspects.says: A lock per object keeps each object consistent, but a reader that takes those locks one at a time can see a total across objects that never existed.
basis: section:A Lock per Bin Keeps Every Move Right and Every Total Wrong

aspects.says: A compareAndSet retry loop that reads the value once, before the loop, spins forever after its first lost race; incrementAndGet or synchronized needs no loop of your own.
basis: section:A compareAndSet Loop That Reads the Value Once Spins Forever; incrementAndGet Leaves No Loop to Get Wrong

aspects.says: An unmodifiable view reads through to the live state, so it changes under its reader; a snapshot is a copy nothing changes.
basis: section:One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting
